newsitem.title: USA: Dow surges to second sharpest gain in history.
newsitem.headline: Dow surges to second sharpest gain in history.

text.p: The Dow industrials surged on Tuesday, as tame inflation data and solid quarterly earnings unleashed a torrent of buying in blue chip issues.
The Dow soared 135 points or 2.1 percent to close unofficially at 6587, a rally that, if official, would stand as the average's second largest ever in point terms.
The gains, when coupled with a 60.21 point rally on Monday, erased more than a quarter of the blue chip average's nearly 700-point decline since it peaked on March 11.
Stocks rallied from the outset of the session, buoyed by a report showing a weaker-than-expected increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) in March.
Investors had been wary of the inflation report in light of the Dow's 148-point decline last Friday. That drop was triggered by news of a stronger-than-expected rise in wholesale prices last month.
"It's a sigh of relief that our worst fears were not materialized," said John Church, chief investment officer at the Glenmede Trust Co.

Stronger-than-expected earnings from several blue chip companies fueled the rally. Dow components Caterpillar Inc and Eastman Kodak Co were among those reporting profits that exceeded Wall Street estimates.
"My argument has been that strong earnings should provide the antidote for this market," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "So far they are."
Shares in Caterpillar rose 3-5/8 to 83 to lead Dow advancers. Kodak shares gained 2 to 75-1/8.
To be sure, there were weak spots in the market, most notably among technology stocks.

Intel Corp dropped 2-3/4 to 131 a day after warning that its revenue growth was likely to slow in the coming quarters. The comments overshadowed the company's strong first-quarter results and cast a pall over the technology group.

A second blow came as Salomon Brothers trimmed its earnings estimates on networking bellwether Cisco Systems Inc. Salomon analyst Peter Swartz said product transitions and general industry sluggishness represented "significant challenges" for Cisco.
Cisco shares slid 3-1/8 to 50-1/8, exacerbating a retreat by technology stocks that dragged the Nasdaq Composite lower.
Analysts said the malaise in the tech sector was symptomatic of a market still reluctant to engage in the widespread buying that marked the bull run of the last two years.

"When you're in a period of rising rates and changing monetary policy, people tend to look closer at the negatives," said Barbara Marcin, vice president at Citibank Global Asset Management. "It's not like a year ago, when people were able to ignore bad news."

Among individual issues, Avant! Corp tumbled 12 to 12-1/2 after the Santa Clara County, Calif., district attorney's office said it filed felony charges against several of the company's senior officials for allegedly stealing Cadence Design Systems Inc technology.
The two companies make software that helps engineers design computer chips and have been bitter rivals. Cadence Design fell 1/2 to 30-1/2.
The S&P 500 index rose 10.99 points to 754.72.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 3.53 points to 1212.88.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
